Simulate a compiled plan

Source: R/simulate.R
sim_run.Rd

Runs a sim_compile() plan over tspan and returns a sim_result.

Usage

sim_run(
  plan,
  tspan,
  times = NULL,
  method = "lsoda",
  rtol = 1e-06,
  atol = 1e-08,
  hmax = NULL,
  maxsteps = 5000,
  initial = NULL,
  include_ticks = TRUE,
  max_events = 1000,
  zc_tol = 1e-09,
  on_failure = c("error", "warn"),
  ...
)

Arguments

plan

A compiled sim_plan.

tspan

Numeric c(start, end).

times

Output times within tspan. Defaults to 201 equally spaced points. Solver output times are independent of the internal steps taken by the integrator.

method

Integration method passed to deSolve::ode(). Models with zero crossings need one of "lsoda", "lsode", "lsodes" or "lsodar". "radau" and "iteration" are refused because they cannot stop at segment boundaries, and "ode23" because its implementation in deSolve can take one uncontrolled step across a whole segment. The fixed-step methods "euler" and "rk4" take steps of at most hmax, by default (tf - t0) / 1000, shortened to end at every boundary and output time.

rtol, atol

Relative and absolute tolerances.

hmax

Optional maximum step size. When the model has events or switching blocks and hmax is not given, it is (tf - t0) / 100 (kinks alone do not set it), because the root finder cannot see two crossings inside one step; give a smaller value for signals that cross faster.

maxsteps

Maximum number of internal steps per segment.

initial

Optional named list overriding initial states, keyed by block name.

include_ticks

Also record a row at every sample hit, so held signals are captured at their changes.

max_events

Maximum number of event and block handler executions before the run is stopped with status "event_limit". Guards against chattering and Zeno behavior.

zc_tol

A zero-crossing function within zc_tol of zero is on its level: arriving there counts as a crossing, the same root is not located again at a restart, and leaving the level fires the event only in its trigger direction (step 5 above). Leaving means moving away from zero; a function that approaches zero inside the band, or stays on it, is watched until it leaves the band, and the event fires then in the direction of the side it leaves on. A function that enters the band without reaching zero (an asymptotic approach) is reported once, at the next segment boundary: with the default band, an event watching exp(-t) falling fires at the first boundary after t = -log(1e-9), about 20.7, which moves when sample clocks add boundaries. The same band decides when a switch control, or the input of compare, sign, floor, ceiling or round, is on its threshold (widened only by the rounding of large values). Use zc_tol = 0 to count exact sign changes only.

on_failure

"error" raises an error when the simulation fails; "warn" returns the partial result with a warning.

...

Further named arguments for deSolve::ode(), such as jactype and jacfunc. A jacfunc receives the absolute time, as the model does. Arguments that set the times, events or root functions (times, events, rootfunc, tcrit, forcings and the compiled code interface) are refused, because simcompR sets them itself.

Value

A sim_result. See sim_signal(), sim_states(), sim_events(), sim_diagnostics() and plot().

Details

Timeline. The interval is cut into segments at every sample hit of a discrete block, every scheduled event time and every breakpoint of a source (for example the time of a step). Sample hits are computed as offset + k * period with integer k, never by accumulating period, so they do not drift and do not depend on where the time axis starts. Two computed times within 16 units in the last place of the largest time in tspan are the same instant; a sample period that is not well above that resolution is an error. The solver integrates each segment on time measured from the segment start, so continuous states keep their accuracy when the time axis starts far from zero.

At an instant (a segment boundary or a located crossing) the simulator, in this order:

  1. runs the handlers of switch, relay and stop blocks whose crossing was located by the solver;

  2. runs the model events due now in increasing priority, then by name: scheduled events, located crossings and crossings caused by a jump of a signal at a segment boundary (a step, a sample hit, a reset). Each event sees the states left by the one before;

  3. evaluates the outputs of all blocks with a sample hit, in execution order, holds them, and then updates the discrete states of those blocks from the same inputs, so a unit delay produces y[k] = u[k-1]; then refreshes the modes of switching blocks;

  4. fires, in further layers, the events whose crossing functions were crossed by steps 2 and 3, comparing each layer with the values before it, until no new crossing occurs. An event does not fire twice in a row from the same layer;

  5. fires block handlers and events whose function sits on its level and moves off it in the trigger direction, found by integrating a short probe (1/1000 of the coming segment), then repeats step 4. So an event can fire at the initial time, and a function whose first derivative is zero there is still seen to move.

A terminal event ends the run after the instant is settled, so other events of the same instant still run. Each handler execution counts toward max_events; a cascade that does not settle ends the run with status "event_limit".

Inside a segment discrete states and held outputs are constant and the continuous states are integrated with deSolve::ode(). The derivative function has no side effects. When zero-crossing functions exist (from sim_add_event(), from switch, relay and stop blocks, or from the kinks of memoryless blocks such as saturation) the root finder stops the solver at the crossing and the instant is handled as above (a kink only restarts the solver). A crossing that ends exactly at zero is not detected again at the restart.

Recording. Signals are computed after the solve from the accepted states, never inside the derivative function. A value recorded at a sample hit is the value after the hit (right-continuous). At an instant where events fire the result has exactly two rows with the same time: the values before the first event and after the last.

Finite values. Block outputs, continuous states and discrete states must stay finite. A block output, reset, sample update or block handler that produces NA, NaN or an infinite value fails the run with a message naming it.

Failure. When the solver fails, a block signals an error or the event limit is reached, the result is marked with a status other than "success" and contains only the times actually reached; no values are extrapolated. With on_failure = "error" (the default for solver and block failures) an error is raised instead.

Statistics. result$diagnostics$stats sums, over all segments, the solver steps, right-hand side evaluations and located roots as reported by deSolve. jacobians counts Jacobian evaluations and LU decompositions for the ODEPACK solvers (lsoda, lsode, lsodes, lsodar, vode, bdf, adams) and is NA for solvers that do not report it.

Examples

m <- sim_model("feedback")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "r", value = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "subtract", "e")
sim_add_block(m, "integrator", "x")
sim_connect(m, "r", "e", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "x", "e", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "e", "x")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), tspan = c(0, 5), times = 0:5)
cbind(numeric = sim_signal(r, "x"), exact = 1 - exp(-(0:5)))
#>        numeric     exact
#> [1,] 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [2,] 0.6321204 0.6321206
#> [3,] 0.8646649 0.8646647
#> [4,] 0.9502131 0.9502129
#> [5,] 0.9816845 0.9816844
#> [6,] 0.9932621 0.9932621
